speaker: Attorney
text: I'd like to turn now to the afternoon of Saturday, May 7, 2016. Do you remember that day?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. I remember it very well. I don't think I'll forget it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Why were you in the area of US-27A and Northeast 140th Court that afternoon?

speaker: Witness B
text: I was waiting for my sister. She was supposed to pick me up at the store there after I finished my shopping.

speaker: Attorney
text: Which store are we talking about?

speaker: Witness B
text: The little store on the corner there, on the south side of the highway. They sell a bit of everything. Feed, drinks, snacks, some hardware.

speaker: Attorney
text: And how did you get to the store that day?

speaker: Witness B
text: A neighbor dropped me off. My car was in the shop that week, so I was getting rides from people.

speaker: Attorney
text: About what time did your neighbor drop you off?

speaker: Witness B
text: Around ten after four. Maybe a minute or two either way.

speaker: Attorney
text: How do you know it was around ten after four?

speaker: Witness B
text: Because my sister texted me she'd be there around five, and I remember thinking I had close to an hour to kill.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did your sister in fact arrive around five?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. Right about five. A little after, maybe, because of everything that was going on by then.

speaker: Attorney
text: We'll get to that later. When you were dropped off, what did you do first?

speaker: Witness B
text: I went inside and did my shopping. I picked up a few things. Some bread, a jug of tea, some batteries, and a bag of birdseed for my mother.

speaker: Attorney
text: About how long were you inside the store?

speaker: Witness B
text: Fifteen minutes, maybe. Not long. It's not a big store.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you pay for your items?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. At the counter.

speaker: Attorney
text: And after you paid, where did you go?

speaker: Witness B
text: I went back outside. Out front of the store, to wait for my sister.

speaker: Attorney
text: Why did you wait outside rather than inside?

speaker: Witness B
text: It was a nice day. And it's a little stuffy in there. I'd rather be outside than stand around in the aisles.

speaker: Attorney
text: So from the time you finished shopping until the collision, you were outside?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. Outside, out front of the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you go back inside the store at any point before the collision?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I stayed outside.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you sit down at any point while you were waiting?

speaker: Witness B
text: Off and on. I can't tell you exactly when. I was mostly standing.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let me ask it differently. At the time of the collision, do you recall whether you were standing or sitting?

speaker: Witness B
text: I was standing.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let's talk about the conditions that afternoon. What was the weather like?

speaker: Witness B
text: Clear. Sunny. No rain at all. It was warm but not hot like summer gets.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were there any clouds that you recall?

speaker: Witness B
text: Maybe a few way off. Nothing over us. It was a bright, clear afternoon.

speaker: Attorney
text: Had it rained earlier that day, to your knowledge?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I know of. The road was dry. Everything was dry.

speaker: Attorney
text: How do you know the road was dry?

speaker: Witness B
text: I could see it. There weren't any puddles, nothing shiny. It looked like a dry road on a sunny day.

speaker: Attorney
text: What about the light? Was it full daylight?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. Full daylight. The sun was still pretty high.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you recall where the sun was in the sky, generally?

speaker: Witness B
text: Up and kind of over to the west. Behind the traffic coming from the west, I'd say. It wasn't down low yet.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was there any haze, smoke, or fog in the area?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. None of that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Any wind that you noticed?

speaker: Witness B
text: A little breeze. Nothing to speak of.

speaker: Attorney
text: Now, how would you describe the traffic on the highway while you were waiting?

speaker: Witness B
text: Light. It's a Saturday afternoon out there. You'd get a few cars, then nothing for a while, then a few more.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were there trucks as well as cars?

speaker: Witness B
text: Some. Mostly cars and pickups. Every so often a bigger truck.

speaker: Attorney
text: Can you estimate how many vehicles passed in, say, a minute?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Calls for speculation.

speaker: Attorney
text: If you can.

speaker: Witness B
text: I really can't give you a number. It wasn't busy. Sometimes a minute would go by and nothing passed at all.

speaker: Attorney
text: What about noise? What could you hear while you were standing outside?

speaker: Witness B
text: The cars going by, mainly. They make that whoosh at highway speed. Some birds. A radio from inside the store when the door opened.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was there any construction or machinery running nearby?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Not that I remember.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was it loud enough that you'd have had trouble hearing someone talk to you?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Only when a truck went by. Otherwise it was pretty quiet out there.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'd like you to describe the road for us in words. We'll look at a map later in the day, but for now, just in your own words. Can you do that?

speaker: Witness B
text: I'll try.

speaker: Attorney
text: Start with the highway itself. How many lanes are there?

speaker: Witness B
text: Four. Two going east and two going west.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is there anything separating the eastbound lanes from the westbound lanes?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. A big grassy median in between. It's wide. Wider than a lot of roads around here.

speaker: Attorney
text: Can you estimate how wide the median is?

speaker: Witness B
text: I'm not good with feet. Wide enough you could park a couple of trucks end to end across it, maybe. Sixty feet? I don't know.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: Fair enough. Which side of the highway is the store on?

speaker: Witness B
text: The south side. The eastbound side.

speaker: Attorney
text: So the lanes nearest the store are the eastbound lanes?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. The eastbound lanes are closest. Then the median, then the westbound lanes on the far side.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is there a place where you can cross the median at that intersection?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. There's a crossover. A cut in the median where you can go across from one side to the other.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is there a traffic light at that crossover?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. No light. No stop light, no blinking light. Just the cut through the median.

speaker: Attorney
text: Are there stop signs?

speaker: Witness B
text: I think there's a stop sign on the side road coming up to the highway. Not on the highway itself.

speaker: Attorney
text: On the highway, are there turn lanes near the crossover?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. There's a left-turn lane on each side, I believe. It's kind of cut into the median before the crossover so people can get out of the fast lane to turn.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let's focus on the westbound side. Is there a left-turn lane for westbound traffic?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. If you're heading west and want to turn left onto 140th, you pull into that turn lane in the median and wait there.

speaker: Attorney
text: And from that westbound turn lane, a vehicle turning left would cross what?

speaker: Witness B
text: It'd go through the crossover and across both of the eastbound lanes, and then onto 140th.

speaker: Attorney
text: Tell me about 140th Court. Which direction does it run from the highway?

speaker: Witness B
text: South. It goes south off the highway, right there by the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: Does 140th Court continue north of the highway?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I've ever seen. I've only ever known it to go south.

speaker: Attorney
text: What's 140th Court like? Is it paved?

speaker: Witness B
text: It's paved. It's a smaller road. Two lanes, one each way, no median. Some houses and fields down it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Where is the store in relation to 140th Court?

speaker: Witness B
text: It's right on the corner. On the east side of 140th, where it meets the highway.

speaker: Attorney
text: So the store sits at the southeast corner of the intersection?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. That's right.

speaker: Attorney
text: Now I'd like to ask about the area to the west of the intersection. What's the land like in that direction?

speaker: Witness B
text: There's a hill. The highway comes over a rise to the west and then comes down toward the intersection.

speaker: Attorney
text: How far west is the top of that hill, roughly?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Foundation.

speaker: Attorney
text: Just your best sense, if you have one.

speaker: Witness B
text: A good ways. A quarter mile maybe. I've never measured it. When you drive it, you come over the top and then you can see the store down the hill in front of you.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is it a steep hill?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Gentle. It's not a big hill. It's just enough that you can't see what's past the top.

speaker: Attorney
text: And when you drive east on that stretch yourself, as you said you do weekly, what do you see when you come over that rise?

speaker: Witness B
text: You see the road go down and the intersection ahead, and the store on the right. It's pretty open from the top on down.

speaker: Attorney
text: What about east of the intersection? What is it like in that direction?

speaker: Witness B
text: Flatter. The highway runs on straight. There are fences, some yards and houses back off the road, some power poles along the side.

speaker: Attorney
text: Are there trees along the highway near the intersection?

speaker: Witness B
text: Some, back from the road. Not right on the shoulder. It's mostly grass along the edges.

speaker: Attorney
text: Are there any buildings at the intersection besides the store?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not right there, no. The store is the main thing. There are houses further off.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is there a parking area at the store?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. A gravel and dirt lot in front and along the side. People pull in off the highway or off 140th.

speaker: Attorney
text: How many cars were parked there while you were waiting?

speaker: Witness B
text: A couple. One or two. It wasn't busy. People would pull in, run in, and leave.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were there any vehicles parked between the store and the highway while you were outside?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I remember. Not big ones. Maybe a car came and went.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'll move on. Is the shoulder of the eastbound lanes paved?

speaker: Witness B
text: There's a paved strip along the edge and then grass. Then the store lot.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is there a speed limit sign anywhere near there that you know of?

speaker: Witness B
text: There's one somewhere back up the road. I believe it's sixty-five out there, but don't hold me to it.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object. Foundation.

speaker: Attorney
text: You're not certain of the posted limit?

speaker: Witness B
text: No, I'm not certain. That's just what I think it is from driving it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let me go back to what you had with you that afternoon. When you went outside after shopping, what were you carrying?

speaker: Witness B
text: My purse, and a shopping bag. One of those plastic bags from the store with my things in it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Just one bag?

speaker: Witness B
text: Just the one. The birdseed was the heaviest thing. I had it all in one bag.

speaker: Attorney
text: Which hand were you holding it in?

speaker: Witness B
text: I'd switch. It was heavy. I think I had it in my left hand most of the time, with my purse on my right shoulder.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you set the bag down at any point?

speaker: Witness B
text: I might have, on and off. I don't remember exactly. When everything happened, I know I still had it, because I remember it banging against my leg when I jumped.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you say you jumped, what do you mean?

speaker: Witness B
text: From the noise. The crash. It made me jump. That's all.

speaker: Attorney
text: We'll come to the crash in detail later. Did you have a cell phone with you that afternoon?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. In my purse.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you using your phone while you were waiting outside?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not right then. Earlier I'd read my sister's text, when I first got there. After that it was in my purse.

speaker: Attorney
text: So in the minutes before the collision, were you looking at your phone?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It was in my purse. I wasn't on it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you talking to anyone on the phone in the minutes before the collision?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I called my sister after. Not before.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you texting, reading, or doing anything with the phone?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I know people will say I was on my phone, but I wasn't. I was just standing there watching the road.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Move to strike the last part as nonresponsive.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you listening to anything? Earbuds, headphones, music?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nothing in my ears.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you wearing glasses that afternoon?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I only wear reading glasses, and those were in my purse.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you need glasses to see things at a distance?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. My distance vision is fine. I just need the readers for small print.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you wearing sunglasses?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I didn't have sunglasses with me that day.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did the sun bother you at all while you were waiting?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It wasn't in my face. I could see fine.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you wearing a hat or anything with a brim?

speaker: Witness B
text: No hat. Just my hair pulled back.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was anyone with you while you were outside?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I was by myself.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you talking with anyone in person while you waited?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not really. A man said hello going into the store. That's about it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you know who that man was?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Never seen him before. Just somebody stopping in.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see where he went after that?

speaker: Witness B
text: Inside. I don't know after that. I wasn't paying him any attention.

speaker: Attorney
text: While you were waiting, what were you doing, generally?

speaker: Witness B
text: Just waiting. Watching the road, watching for my sister's car. She'd be coming from the west, so I kept looking that way.

speaker: Attorney
text: Why would your sister be coming from the west?

speaker: Witness B
text: Because she lives west of there. She'd come down the highway over that hill, same as anybody coming from that direction.

speaker: Attorney
text: So you were watching westbound or eastbound traffic for her?

speaker: Witness B
text: Eastbound. She'd be heading east toward me, coming down the hill.

speaker: Attorney
text: What kind of car does your sister drive?

speaker: Witness B
text: A little silver hatchback. I was looking for that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you watch the cars that came over the hill while you waited?

speaker: Witness B
text: Every one of them. Every time something came over I'd look to see if it was her.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was there anything that afternoon, before the collision, that seemed unusual to you about the traffic?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It was just a normal afternoon. Cars going by. Nothing unusual until it happened.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you notice any vehicles pulling into or out of the store lot in the few minutes before the collision?

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't remember any right then. It was quiet.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you notice anyone walking along the highway, or crossing it?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nobody walking.

speaker: Attorney
text: Any bicycles or motorcycles?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I remember.

speaker: Attorney
text: Any emergency vehicles, police cars, anything with lights, before the collision?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Not before. Afterward, yes, a lot of them.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let me ask one more general question about where you were. Throughout the time you were waiting, where were you?

speaker: Witness B
text: Outside. Out front of the store. I've said that.

speaker: Attorney
text: You have. I'm just making sure the record is clear. Did you go around to the side or back of the store at any point?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I stayed out front.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you walk out toward the highway at any point before the collision?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I stayed by the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you cross 140th Court at any point before the collision?

speaker: Witness B
text: No.

speaker: Attorney
text: Had you ever waited outside that store before, on another day?

speaker: Witness B
text: A few times. When I've gotten rides. It's an easy place for people to pick me up.

speaker: Attorney
text: So you were familiar with what the intersection looks like from the store?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. I know what it looks like from there.

speaker: Attorney
text: Before May 7, had you ever seen a collision at that intersection?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Never. I'd heard people say it's a bad crossing, but I'd never seen anything.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object. Move to strike as hearsay.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'll ask you just about what you saw yourself. Before that day, had you yourself seen any near misses there?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I can remember. Nothing that stuck with me.

speaker: Attorney
text: All right. In the minutes leading up to the collision, about how long had you been standing outside?

speaker: Witness B
text: Ten minutes. Maybe a little more. I'd finished shopping at around twenty-five after, so ten or twelve minutes.

speaker: Attorney
text: And how are you estimating that?

speaker: Witness B
text: From when I got there and how long I was inside. I didn't look at a clock. It's my best guess.

speaker: Attorney
text: Understood. Did anything distract you in those minutes before? Any noise, anything that pulled your attention away from the road?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nothing like that. I was just looking at the road for my sister.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you hungry, tired, not feeling well, anything of that sort that day?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I felt fine. I'd had lunch. I was a little tired from the week, but nothing out of the ordinary.

speaker: Attorney
text: Had you had anything to drink that day other than water or tea?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Tea and water. That's all.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you taking any medication that affects your vision or your memory?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nothing like that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. I think that covers the background of the afternoon. Next I want to move to the traffic you saw coming from the west, beginning with the first time you noticed the car. Before I do, is there anything about the conditions or the road we've discussed that you want to add or correct?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I think I've said it. It was clear, it was quiet, and I was out front waiting.
